sections.text:
تستخدم هذه الطريقة لتبين مدى جودة الزيت كمادة عازلة "لاتسمح بمرور التيار 
 الكهربى خلاله" ويتوقف هذا القياس على كيفية تمثيل عينة الزيت فى الدائرة 
 الكهربية.

قام بإعداد هذا المستند 
 الكيميائية/ حنان محمد 
 على حمودة وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/
 خالد بسطاوى مكى محسب وقام بالاختبار السيد المشرف 
 الفنى/ 
 جمال احمد اسماعيل وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/ 
 محمد وجدى عبد الله 
 مدير عام بمحطة كهرباء السد العالى بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء وموثق من المهندس/ 
 عبد النبى عبد الغنى عبد النبى 
 رئيس قطاع المحطة بشركة 
 المحطات المائية 
 لإنتاج الكهرباء.

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/ 
 محمد اسامة سليمان سليم منسق الـMPIS بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء.

تأكد من صحة البيانات الواردة 
 على العينة.

التأكد من وضع 
 العينة فى الصندوق الخاص بها لعدم تعرضها لضوء الشمس والاتربة .
التأكد من ان زجاجة العينة جافة (خالية من المياه والاتربة).

التأكد من اختيار طريقة القياس المطلوبة من على 
 شاشة الجهاز وكذلك درجة 
 الحرارة المطلوبة.
يجب التأكد من توصيل الارضى بالجهاز.
عند اجراء الاختبار نتجنب انسكاب الزيت على الارض وان حدث ذلك يتم ازالته.

جهاز قياس ظل زاوية الفقد
 Tan 
 δ
اخذ 45 مل من الزيت المراد اختباره فى مخبار نظيف تماما.

تفريغ الزيت من المخبار فى انبوبة الملئ بالجهاز عن 
 طريق قمع صغير حتى العلامة والانتظار حتى يرتفع الزيت فى انبوبة التهوية 
 ويستمر الملئ حتى 45 مل.
تفريغ الزيت والانتظار حتى يتوقف نزوله من الخرطوم.

يعاد الملىء 
 من جديد كما سبق 1-3 بنفس الزيت المراد اختباره.

الضغط على مفتاح المختص بإظهار 
 البيانات الخاصة بالقياس على الشاشة ثم اختيار درجة الحرارة المراد قياس 
 العينة عندها (20-70-90) م
الضغط على المفتاح المختص ببدء القياس .
ننتظر حتى الحصول على نتائج القياس مطبوعة.

 على جهاز قياس ظل زاوية الفقد Tan

sections_en.text: This method is used to show the quality of the oil as an insulating material ("does not allow electric current to pass through it"); this measurement depends on how the oil sample is represented in the electric circuit.

This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Khaled Bastawy Makki Mohasseb, tested by the technical supervisor Gamal Ahmed Ismail, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: An increase in the dissipation angle value for insulating liquids indicates oil contamination with moisture, impurities and oxidation products, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material.
When a capacitor is connected in an electric circuit, the current passing through this capacitor will lead the circuit voltage by 90°.
If we consider that the oil sample to be tested is placed between the two plates of this capacitor (as an insulating material) and is 100% insulating, then the capacitive current at that time is Ic.

Since an ideal insulating material sometimes cannot exist, especially at high temperatures of 70-90°C, there is a deviation of the capacitive current from the ideal position by a small angle δ to Ic′ (which is the dissipation angle being measured). In practice, the tangent of this angle is measured; since this angle is very small, the tangent of the angle is considered to be the angle itself. It is noted from the diagram that the smallness or largeness of the angle indicates the quality of the oil as an insulating material.
Note: this measurement is carried out for Russian oils at 20-70°C and for other oils at 90°C.
It is the very small angle between the capacitive current Ic and its deviation Ic′; due to the smallness of this angle, the tangent of the angle is the angle itself: Tan δ = δ.
Dissipation angle "δ"
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2).
Make sure the data on the sample are correct.
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust.
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust).
Make sure to select the required measurement method from the apparatus screen, as well as the required temperature.
Make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it.
Dissipation factor (Tan δ) measuring apparatus
Take 45 ml of the oil to be tested in a completely clean cylinder.
Empty the oil from the cylinder into the filling tube of the apparatus through a small funnel, up to the mark, and wait until the oil rises in the vent tube; continue filling up to 45 ml.
Empty the oil and wait until it stops coming down from the hose.
Refill again as before, steps 1-3, with the same oil to be tested.
Press the key for displaying the measurement data on the screen, then select the temperature at which the sample is to be measured (20-70-90)°C.
Press the key for starting the measurement.
Wait until the measurement results are printed.
Note: this test is carried out on a dissipation factor (Tan δ) measuring apparatus, model DTL-2A - Austria No. 415-015, manufactured by BAUR-Austria.

Introduction
This method is used to show the quality of the oil as an insulating material ("does not allow electric current to pass through it"); this measurement depends on how the oil sample is represented in the electric circuit.
This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Khaled Bastawy Makki Mohasseb, tested by the technical supervisor Gamal Ahmed Ismail, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
An increase in the dissipation angle value for insulating liquids indicates oil contamination with moisture, impurities and oxidation products, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material. | 1.
Measurement Theory
 | When a capacitor is connected in an electric circuit, the current passing through this capacitor will lead the circuit voltage by 90°. | 1.
If we consider that the oil sample to be tested is placed between the two plates of this capacitor (as an insulating material) and is 100% insulating, then the capacitive current at that time is Ic. | 2.
Since an ideal insulating material sometimes cannot exist, especially at high temperatures of 70-90°C, there is a deviation of the capacitive current from the ideal position by a small angle δ to Ic′ (which is the dissipation angle being measured). In practice, the tangent of this angle is measured; since this angle is very small, the tangent of the angle is considered to be the angle itself. It is noted from the diagram that the smallness or largeness of the angle indicates the quality of the oil as an insulating material. | 3.
Note: this measurement is carried out for Russian oils at 20-70°C and for other oils at 90°C.
Definition
It is the very small angle between the capacitive current Ic and its deviation Ic′; due to the smallness of this angle, the tangent of the angle is the angle itself: Tan δ = δ. | Dissipation angle "δ"
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2). | 
Make sure the data on the sample are correct. | 
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust. | 
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust). | 
Make sure to select the required measurement method from the apparatus screen, as well as the required temperature. | 
Environmental Recommendations
Make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus. | 1.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it. | 2.
Tools and Equipment Used
Dissipation factor (Tan δ) measuring apparatus | 1.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Take 45 ml of the oil to be tested in a completely clean cylinder. | 1.
Empty the oil from the cylinder into the filling tube of the apparatus through a small funnel, up to the mark, and wait until the oil rises in the vent tube; continue filling up to 45 ml. | 2.
Empty the oil and wait until it stops coming down from the hose. | 3.
Refill again as before, steps 1-3, with the same oil to be tested. | 4.
Press the key for displaying the measurement data on the screen, then select the temperature at which the sample is to be measured (20-70-90)°C. | 5.
Press the key for starting the measurement. | 6.
Wait until the measurement results are printed. | 7.
Note: this test is carried out on a dissipation factor (Tan δ) measuring apparatus, model DTL-2A - Austria No. 415-015, manufactured by BAUR-Austria.
